newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Norwich Union says Irish business up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Norwich Union says Irish business up in 1996.

text.p: Norwich Union Life and Pensions said on Wednesday that its new annual and single premium business had increased by 24 and 28 percent respectively in 1996.
The company said new annual premium business grew to 15.8 million punts last year while single premium business rose to 19.2 million punts.

This gives a total annual premium equivalent of 17.7 million Irish pounds, an increase of 25 percent on 1995, Norwich Union said in a statement. Total in force business grew by 10 percent to 120 million punts, it added.

On the annual premium side, protection and savings business accounted for 9.1 million and pensions business for 6.7 million punts. Single premium pension sales totalled 13.0 million with the balance of 6.2 million due to single premium investment products, the company said.

"The substantial increase in our new business figures reflects our policy of providing value for money products in the protection, savings and pensions markets," Grant Barrans, general manager of life and pensions, said in the statement.
He added that the company had launched a new suite of unit-linked pension plans this week.
